result.title: Beyond Temporal Overlap: Consumer-Aware Evaluation of Sign-Language Segmentation across Three Corpora
result.comment: Submitted to IEEE FG 2027. 9 pages, 4 figures. Supplementary material included
result.summary: Sign-language segmentation divides continuous signing into clips. In this study, the downstream consumer is a frozen recognizer that assigns one sign label to each predicted clip. Existing metrics instead compare predicted clips with manually annotated boundaries. They do not directly measure whether a clip preserves the visual evidence needed by the recognizer or whether the segmenter produces too many clips. We therefore ask whether overlap metrics and this consumer prefer the same segmenter. We evaluate 27 outputs from three segmentation architectures, three random seeds, and three corpora. Controlled boundary edits separate the effect of removing sign evidence from that of adding surrounding context. Overlap predicts recognition on average, but it does not always determine model choice. At the same intersection-over-union, different recognizers can prefer the shorter or the longer clip. The real outputs reveal two operating regimes. On DGS, overlap, recognition, and sequence error select the same model. On BSL, recognition-based selection recovers and recognizes more reference signs but increases word error rate (WER). Dicta-Sign shows the reverse trade-off: WER selection reduces in-vocabulary WER by 31.17 points but misses more recognizable signs. Segmenters should therefore be evaluated on four axes: temporal agreement, reference recovery, clip recognition, and sequence error, rather than on overlap alone.

AI.brief_summary: 论文以冻结手语识别器作为下游消费者，跨三个语料和三种分割架构评估手语分段输出，比较重叠度指标与识别效果是否选择同一模型，并通过受控边界编辑分离「删去证据」与「加入上下文」的影响。
AI.relevance_reason: 其核心是以下游消费者检验中间片段是否保留任务所需视觉证据，而非仅与人工标注对齐，这一评价视角可能可供核查 latent 状态中视觉证据保留度的度量设计，但与 LVR 生成机制无直接关联。
